topics.label: Almería and Campo de Níjar fluvial restoration
topics.description: A formally assigned restoration works project for 56 ramblas in three sectors: Almería, Campo de Níjar–Artal and Cabo de Gata. The December 2022 assignment to TRAGSA combines removal of agro-waste/construction debris and invasive exotic vegetation, conveyance improvements and bank defence with native riparian planting of certified provenance. It also provides for an interpreted public river path on lower Rambla Morales in the Cabo de Gata–Níjar protected area. The maximum assigned budget is EUR 3,866,930.52, with an initial 24-month period and PRTR C4.I3 financing. These records establish an assignment and delivery obligations, not completed hectares or measured ecological recovery. Separate 2023 supervision and 2024 plant-supply documents retain their own roles and dates.

topics.label: Níjar works supervision and environmental surveillance
topics.description: The June 2023 TRAGSATEC assignment separately covers assistance to works direction, health/safety coordination and environmental surveillance for the Almería/Campo de Níjar project. Surveillance must check implementation and effectiveness of protective/corrective measures, investigate unsatisfactory performance, detect unanticipated impacts and report to works direction and the environmental authority. The assignment budget is EUR 151,606.30. Its initial 24-month period starts with the works and can extend through completion and required documentation. Monthly certification and PRTR milestone reports are delivery controls; this document does not provide the monitoring results. Its inconsistent subcontracting statements remain unresolved.

topics.label: Campo de Níjar native plant supply roster
topics.description: The 8 August 2024 TSA0078436 specification requests plants for planting and replacement of failures in the semi-arid fluvial-restoration works. Two lots list 22 named taxa in 23 supply rows, including two container sizes for Populus alba. Carob appears as 1,376 units in 1 L nursery containers; jujube as 9,407 units in 1 L containers. These are requested supply quantities and nursery stock volumes, not confirmed installed plants, an ecological association, reservoir capacity or irrigation doses. Lot 2 is expressly described as native species of the Levante Almeriense. The contract imposes provenance, plant health, root architecture and delivery acceptance requirements. Source spellings and uncertain taxonomy remain visible; no working community or plant count is changed.

topics.label: Níjar stock provenance and traceability
topics.description: The supply specification requires accredited nursery material from ecologically similar areas, identifying Murciano-Almeriense origin and provenance region 38. For shrub/scrub/climber species without a legally established region, it requires Almeriense district biogeographic provenance in the described collection/propagation circumstances. In the absence of the preferred material, region 36 is exceptionally permitted for Populus alba and Populus nigra; the mention of P. nigra in that exception does not put it in the supply roster. Provenance must be certified to TRAGSA with accompanying documentation/label, and a phytosanitary passport and health check are required. These are project-specification conditions, not a present universal legal determination.

source_refs.label: Plant provenance: accredited nursery and region 38
Provenance exceptions, certification, map and plant passport

topics.label: Níjar nursery-stock quality and acceptance
topics.description: The specification requires balanced healthy shoots/roots and rejects disease, insect damage, dehydration, wounds and strongly deformed roots. Containers must prevent root spiralling and root rebound; stock raised at least 10 cm above ground is specified for aerial root pruning. The document also describes stock age, container/plug integrity and substrate porosity of 60–80%, with relatively moist planting substrate. TRAGSA approves or rejects material on receipt. These procurement requirements explain establishment risk controls; they are not measured effects, species-specific planting recipes or a numerical watering regime. The generic size/age provisions and the specific supply-row container volumes retain their own context.

findings.label: Níjar: requested plant quantities and stock formats
findings.text: The two-lot supply roster is retained as 23 rows for 22 taxa. It includes 1,376 Ceratonia siliqua in 1 L containers, 4,800 Pistacia lentiscus in at least 250 cc cells, 7,364 Nerium oleander and 9,407 Ziziphus lotus in 1 L containers. Populus alba has separate 1,356 × 1 L and 912 × 10 L rows. These are procurement quantities, not planting completion or a working-community census. Nursery container volume is not a reservoir refill or irrigation dose. Other rows are preserved in the linked structured aspects and exact source tables.

findings.label: Níjar: works and supervision are separate assignments
findings.text: Works assignment 6/2022/ES gives EUR 3,866,930.52 using non-VAT-subject TRAGSA 2022 tariffs, plus a separate 10% measurement-excess reserve of EUR 386,693.05. The stated works period is 24 months from its resolution. Supervision assignment 1/2023/ES gives EUR 151,606.30 using TRAGSA 2023 tariffs and a period beginning with works, linked to completion/document delivery. Both identify PRTR C4.I3, but their budgets, roles and dates are distinct. The sources do not report actual expenditure or achieved hectares.

findings.label: Cost comparison is an administrative estimate, not field performance
findings.text: The works assignment compares its tariff-based EUR 3,866,930.52 cost with a hypothetical tender result of EUR 3,970,645.02 and states 2.68% efficiency relative to the assignment. This is the issuing administration’s economic justification using assumed market/tender coefficients, not an observed competitive award, realized saving or ecological outcome.
